newsitem.title: UK: Brazil, Thailand feature on sugar freight market.
newsitem.headline: Brazil, Thailand feature on sugar freight market.

text.p: Fresh and fixed business continued apace on London's sugar freight market on Thursday with Brazil and Thailand once again featuring prominently as origins, shipbrokers said.
E D F & Man appeared a number of times in the day's business, issuing two new orders and fixing one from earlier in the week.
Man quoted for 6,500/8,000 tonnes of bagged sugar from Santos to west Africa for prompt shipment and 19/20,000 tonnes in bulk from Recife or Maceio to US Gulf/Atlantic for mid-June dates.
Shipbrokers said Man fully fixed its earlier order for 12,500 tonnes of bagged sugar from Immingham to Tunisia, also for mid-June, at a rate believed to in the low to mid-$30 bracket.
The other main player on Thursday was Genoc, which also issued two new orders and fixed a bulk sugar cargo.

Genoc quoted for 16,500/17,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Maputo to Kantvik for mid-June and a further 12/12,500 tonnes from Thailand to Vladivostok for 10 days notice. Details of the rates have yet to emerge.
It fixed around 13,000 tonnes in bulk from Maputo to Nantes for prompt shipment, market sources said.
Other firmer business to emerge included Louis Dreyfys, said to have fixed 12,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Thailand to south China for the end of June.
Shipbrokers said Jean Lion fixed a prompt 24/25,000 tonnes, again in bulk, from Cuba to Morocco with options of Mediterranean, Black Sea and Baltic.
